text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Shadow foreign minister Guido de Marco urges government, opposed to Malta joining the European Union, not to take EU decisions before end of the EU Inter-Governmental Conference.
- Sliema car park, in Malta's second biggest city, closed by the Planning Authority for allegedly not conforming to building permit conditions.
- Two more to join Hilton hunger strike, started on Monday by protesters who want a government inquiry into a Hilton hotel building project which they say will harm the environment.
- Dangerous microbe found in hospital's intensive therapy unit.

- Workers at Qawra Palace Hotel support the General Workers Union. Union and the four-star hotel have been in dispute for weeks over union recognition. Workers cast their ballot in favour of the union on Wednesday.
